faq.question: Q1. What is the last date to apply for the IIT (ISM) Dhanbad recruitment?
faq.answer: The last date to submit the online application form for the IIT (ISM) Dhanbad recruitment is 15 September 2026.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available for Junior Research Fellow (JRF) / Senior Research Fellow (SRF) and Postdoctoral Fellow (PDF) posts?
faq.answer: There are a total of 3 vacancies available for these positions.

faq.question: Q3. What is the educational qualification required for the JRF/SRF post?
faq.answer: For JRF/SRF, candidates need to have M.E./M.Tech or B.E./B.Tech in CSE/IT/AI/ECE/EE/allied branches with specific marks and GATE/NET qualification. SRF requires two years of research experience.

faq.question: Q4. What is the educational qualification for the Postdoctoral Fellow (PDF) position?
faq.answer: For the PDF position, candidates must have a PhD in CSE/IT/AI/ECE/EE/allied branches with a minimum of 60% marks, GATE/NET qualification, and at least one SCI Journal publication.

faq.question: Q5. Is there any application fee for this recruitment?
faq.answer: No, there is no application fee mentioned for any category (General/OBC, SC/ST) for this recruitment.

faq.question: Q6. What is the salary structure for the JRF and SRF posts?
faq.answer: The salary for JRF is Rs. 37,000 per month + 20% HRA, and for SRF, it is Rs. 42,000 per month + 20% HRA.

faq.question: Q7. What is the salary for the Postdoctoral Fellow (PDF) position?
faq.answer: The salary for the Postdoctoral Fellow (PDF) is Rs. 77,000 per month + 20% HRA.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for these positions?
faq.answer: The selection process for these positions will be based on an Interview.

faq.question: Q9. What is the mode of application for the IIT (ISM) Dhanbad recruitment?
faq.answer: The application process is entirely online.

faq.question: Q10. Where can I find the official notification and apply online?
faq.answer: You can find the links to the official notification and the online application form in the "Important Links" section of this article.
